details: Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has experienced billions in net customer withdrawals, with some reports indicating over $7 billion in 24-hour outflows from linked wallets, following a record $6.3 billion hack attributed to North Korea's TraderTraitor group. Binance has since reopened withdrawals, stating it has replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets. The incident has raised significant concerns about the security of centralized exchanges.
title: Binance Faces Billions in Withdrawals Post-$6.3B Hack; Restores Services

details: Bitcoin (BTC) is trading around $78,000, showing a modest recovery after dipping following the Binance hack. The broader crypto market also saw some stabilization on November 2nd, with the CeFi sector experiencing gains. However, this follows a challenging October for Bitcoin, which marked its second consecutive monthly loss.
title: Bitcoin Stabilizes Around $78K Amid Modest Market Recovery

details: U.S. spot Bitcoin and Ether exchange-traded funds (ETFs) collectively recorded a substantial net outflow of $716 million on November 2nd. Bitcoin ETFs alone accounted for $614 million of these outflows, while Ether ETFs saw $102 million depart. This continues a trend of cautious investor sentiment reflected in significant outflows over the past week and late October.
title: US Bitcoin and Ether ETFs See Significant Outflows on November 2

details: South Korea is reportedly considering postponing the implementation of its 22% cryptocurrency tax until 2029. This potential delay could provide more breathing room for the domestic crypto industry and investors.
title: South Korea Considers Delaying Crypto Tax to 2029

details: As part of its recent budget, the UK government has confirmed plans to introduce legislation in Finance Bill 2026–27 to treat certain stablecoins more like traditional money for tax purposes. This proposal, if approved, is expected to take effect in April 2027 and aims to provide clearer tax guidelines for stablecoins that maintain their value against fiat currencies and are designed for payment use.
title: UK Proposes Money-Like Tax Treatment for Eligible Stablecoins
